brief.intro: New to this project type? A pharmaceutical / life-sciences plant manufactures drug products or active ingredients inside classified cleanrooms under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP). Unlike a normal industrial building, construction completion is not the finish line — every system must be formally qualified (Installation, Operational and Performance Qualification) and every room classified before it can be used. Clean utilities (purified water, water-for-injection, clean steam, compressed gases) and cleanroom HVAC — particle counts and pressure cascades — are the schedule drivers, not the structure. Your schedule stands or falls on treating qualification as real, deliverable-based duration and never letting production start creep up against it.

scope.name: Structure & shell
scope.desc: Foundations, frame, envelope and roof — weather-tight before cleanroom fit-out begins.

scope.name: Cleanroom fit-out
scope.desc: Wall/ceiling/floor systems, hygienic doors, pass-throughs and airlocks — a functional system, not a finish.

scope.name: Cleanroom HVAC
scope.desc: AHUs, HEPA/ULPA filtration, pressure cascades, temperature & humidity control.

scope.name: Clean utilities
scope.desc: Purified water (PW), water-for-injection (WFI), clean steam, compressed gases (nitrogen, CDA, oxygen).

scope.name: Process equipment & skids
scope.desc: Bioreactors/tanks, process skids, Clean-in-Place / Sterilise-in-Place (CIP/SIP) systems.

scope.name: Electrical & BMS
scope.desc: Power distribution, UPS for critical loads, building management system for environmental monitoring.

scope.name: Automation & controls
scope.desc: Process automation (DCS/PLC/SCADA) and data-integrity (21 CFR Part 11) configuration.

scope.name: Commissioning, qualification & validation
scope.desc: Cleanroom classification, IQ/OQ/PQ and process validation — the real handover gate.

glossary.plain: Good Manufacturing Practice — the regulatory quality standard the facility must be built and operated to.
the particle-count standard a room must achieve and hold.
Installation / Operational / Performance Qualification — the staged proof that equipment is installed right, works right, and performs right.
high-purity water grades used in drug manufacturing, produced and distributed to strict quality limits.
steam generated from purified water, used to sterilise equipment (SIP).
Clean-in-Place / Sterilise-in-Place — automated cleaning and sterilising of process equipment without taking it apart.
rooms held at different air pressures, cleanest highest, so air only ever flows from clean to less-clean.
the regulation governing electronic records and signatures in the automation system.

must_get_right: It's validation-led, not just construction-led — a system is only done when IQ/OQ/PQ is signed off; build CQV time into the programme as real duration, not a formality at the end.
Cleanroom finishes and HVAC are functional systems, not cosmetic — sequence them so the room can be classified (particle count, pressure cascade) before equipment moves in.
Clean utilities (PW/WFI/clean steam/gases) must be qualified before process equipment can be qualified — treat them as a hard predecessor, not parallel scope.
Protect the validation float — regulatory review and protocol re-test cycles are common; never schedule production start immediately after PQ with no buffer.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Qualification activities (IQ/OQ/PQ) are scheduled as real-duration activities with their own logic and deliverables (protocol write-up, execution, report) — never as zero-duration milestones.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and structure run a 6-day week; cleanroom fit-out and clean-utility installation run controlled, typically single-shift, conditions to protect quality. Qualification execution follows a fixed protocol-approval cycle — write → review → approve → execute → report — that cannot be compressed by adding shifts.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs cleanroom envelope & fit-out → HVAC & clean-utility installation → system commissioning → cleanroom classification → Installation Qualification → Operational Qualification → Performance Qualification → process validation → regulatory sign-off. Process-equipment installation runs in parallel with utilities but cannot itself be qualified until the utilities it depends on (clean steam, WFI, gases) are already qualified.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: User requirement specifications (URS) and design are frozen before cleanroom fit-out starts; qualification protocols are pre-approved by Quality before execution; a single validation campaign with no major protocol failures; regulatory inspection is scheduled after PQ completion.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Cleanroom areas require strict access and gowning control from fit-out completion onward; specialist qualification (CQV) engineers and Quality Assurance reviewers are a constrained, shared resource across the validation phase; material and personnel flow must respect the classified-area pressure cascade even during construction close-out.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: protocol deviations during IQ/OQ/PQ requiring re-execution, cleanroom classification failure (particle count or pressure) forcing rework, and regulatory review comments extending the validation float. Schedule contingency is held around the qualification phase (IQ→PQ) and before regulatory sign-off, not spread across construction.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for fit-out/utilities works and qualification execution — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
